output.normalized_title: ingress-lb: OOMKilled exit code 137 on worker pods (ingress-lb)
symptoms: OOMKilled exit code 137 on worker pods

output.classification_reasoning: The ingress load balancer's worker pods were terminated with OOMKilled (exit code 137), indicating that the application layer ran out of memory rather than a network, authentication, database, or storage capacity issue. The failure is tied to the ingress-lb service's runtime behavior, which is an application component. The incident impacted 15,000 users and lasted 72 minutes, suggesting that remediation required investigation of pod memory limits, resource requests, and possibly code paths causing memory bloat. While the root cause is confined to the application tier, the need to analyze pod configurations, memory profiling, and coordination across the load‑balancing stack adds moderate operational effort, placing the incident in the "Moderate" complexity tier.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

recurring_patterns.symptom_pattern: OOMKilled exit code 137 on worker pods

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: A similar OOMKilled symptom was observed in a historical log for inventory‑api, but no prior incident matches the ingress‑lb service. Correlation is limited to symptom similarity; further root‑cause analysis is required.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 5,000 users or outage >= 120 minutes.
output.justification: The incident affects a Tier-1 service with 15,000 users impacted, which exceeds the 5,000‑user threshold defined in the SLA. Although the outage duration (72 minutes) is below the 120‑minute time threshold, the user impact alone satisfies the rule for SEV-1. Therefore, per the deterministic severity rule, the incident must be classified as SEV-1.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access, Context, and Write‑Freeze
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has the required ProdOperations role, the kubectl context points to the production cluster, and a write‑freeze is in place to prevent data loss during node operations.
verification: Context output matches prod-us-east-1
AWS identity shows role ProdOperations
Write‑freeze endpoint returns {"freeze":true}

remediation_steps.title: Identify OOM‑Killed Pods and Node Memory Pressure
remediation_steps.description: List the pods that were OOMKilled, determine the node(s) they ran on, and check node memory metrics to confirm resource exhaustion.
commands: kubectl get pods -n ingress -l app=ingress-lb -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.status.containerStatuses[0].state.terminated.reason}{"\n"}{end}' | grep OOMKilled
kubectl top pods -n ingress | grep ingress-lb
verification: List of OOMKilled pods captured
Node memory usage > 90% on affected node(s)

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica and Drain Affected Node(s)
remediation_steps.description: Promote the standby read‑replica of the ingress‑lb data store to primary, then safely cordon and drain the node experiencing OOM to allow pod rescheduling with fresh resources.
verification: RDS endpoint now points to promoted replica (describe-db-instances shows Primary)
Node status shows SchedulingDisabled
All ingress‑lb pods rescheduled and show READY=1/1

remediation_steps.title: Apply Updated Resource Requests/Limits and Restart Pods
remediation_steps.description: Patch the deployment to increase memory requests/limits for the worker containers, then perform a rolling restart to apply the new spec.
verification: Deployment spec reflects new memory values
All pods reach READY=1/1 without OOMKilled events in the last 10 minutes

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks, verify traffic flow, and confirm that error logs have returned to baseline levels.
commands: kubectl logs deployment/ingress-lb -n ingress --tail=100 | grep -i panic
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200 with body 'OK'
No panic logs in the last 15 minutes
Load balancer reports healthy backend count equal to desired replica count

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert deployment to the previous container image tag, restore original memory requests/limits, and, if needed, roll back the read‑replica promotion by failing over to the original primary.

steps.description: Undo deployment image and resource changes
verification: Deployment revision returns to previous image tag
Resource specs match pre‑remediation values

steps.description: Failover back to original primary database (if promotion caused issues)
verification: RDS endpoint resolves to original primary instance
No replication lag reported

steps.description: Uncordon and restore original node scheduling (in case drain caused service degradation)
verification: Node scheduling re-enabled and Ready status is true

commands: kubectl get pods -n ingress -l app=ingress-lb -o wide
verification: Health endpoint returns HTTP 200
All pods are Running and Ready

prerequisite_checks: Rollback procedures documented and approved by change management
post_execution_checks: All verification steps passed for each remediation action
No new OOMKilled events observed for 15 minutes post‑restart
